sources.entry: It's time to start writing explains why Jeff Bezos banned PowerPoint at Amazon.

summary.title: It's time to start writing
summary.one_liner: Writing a structured narrative forces clearer thinking than slides, and it helps engineers persuade teams to reach technical decisions.
takeaways: Amazon's 2004 policy replaced PowerPoint with multi-page written narratives read at the start of meetings.
The value lies in the act of writing: it forces better structure, prioritisation and understanding of how ideas relate.
Unstructured group debate can produce learning but often no consensus; a single coherent narrative can break the stalemate.
A good technology-choice narrative covers the reasons for change, alternatives, risks, transition, and ends with a recommendation tied to business needs.
Clear written thinking carries over to oral explanations and lets an author adapt to any audience.
summary.summary: The author starts from Jeff Bezos's 2004 email banning PowerPoint at Amazon in favour of written narratives, and argues the point is about thinking rather than reading. Using a hypothetical team choosing between Kubernetes and Nomad, the post walks through the questions a written narrative should answer, from the business motivation and stakes to risks, transition and a final recommendation. It concludes that writing clarifies the author's own thinking, which makes them more persuasive and better able to explain ideas orally to any audience. The post is an opinion essay with no code.
